name: Harvest Sheet-Pan Chicken with Sweet Potatoes and Brussels Sprouts
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 316 cal / 30g protein using breasts and no starch; our build swaps in thighs and raises the portion, landing near 520 - est_cal is MINE, confidence medium. Included because the catalog has almost no true sheet-pan dinner and all four vegetables are tracked board ids. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast: WAVE-4: spec note says thighs, build had breast - swapped, grams kept (4 pieces ~800 g)
intro_html: People call sheet-pan dinners lazy. I call them efficient. Chicken, sweet potatoes, brussels sprouts, red onion and apple all roast on the same hot metal while you go do something more interesting, and the oven does the browning that a skillet would make you earn one batch at a time. Each container lands 568 calories and 53 grams of protein for about $3.85 (at everyday cost). There is a good reason that number sits where it does, and I will tell you exactly what it is in a minute.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 7.5 lb: ~$13.11. Buy 8 lbs: $14.16.
Pantry seasonings (italian seasoning, ground cinnamon, salt, black pepper): ~$1.70. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $34.49 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.46 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $39.81 across 14 servings, roughly $2.84 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $14.13 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $53.94. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.85 a bowl (at everyday cost). That is our expensive end and I am not going to dress it up. Chicken thighs and a small hill of brussels sprouts are the two lines doing the damage, and between them they account for most of what you spend. The upside is you can see both of them in every container.
shop_smart: Brussels sprouts are the biggest produce line in this recipe by a wide margin. Buy them loose by the pound instead of trimmed in a bag, and buy them in fall and winter when they are in season and the per-pound price falls through the floor.

Chicken thighs are the other heavy line. The big club packs run cheaper per pound than the tray packs, so buy the biggest pack you will use before it turns. Thighs are already the budget cut here, and they stay juicy in a hot oven where breast would dry out.
Sweet potatoes and red onion are the cheap seats here. Buy them by the bag rather than by the each, since the bag price per pound is almost always better and both keep for weeks in a cool cabinet.
Skip the fancy apples. You want a firm variety that holds its shape in a hot oven, and the loose bin apples do that just as well as the ones with a sticker and a story.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F with racks in the upper and lower thirds, and pull out two large sheet pans.

Peel and cube the sweet potatoes. Toss them with a third of the olive oil, some italian seasoning, the cinnamon, salt and pepper, spread them on one pan, and give them a 15 minute head start in the oven.

While those roast, halve the brussels sprouts, cut the red onion into thick wedges, and core and chop the apples. Toss all three with another third of the oil, more italian seasoning, salt and pepper.
Cut the chicken into large chunks and toss with the last of the oil, the minced garlic, the rest of the italian seasoning, salt and pepper.
Pull the sweet potato pan, push the potatoes to one side, and add the sprouts, onion and apple. Spread the chicken in a single layer on the second pan so it roasts instead of steams.
Roast both pans 18 to 22 minutes, swapping racks halfway, until the chicken reads 165F and the sprouts are dark and crispy at the leaf edges.
Scrape everything into your big mixing pot, pan juices included, and fold it together so the cinnamon and the sweet potato starch coat the whole thing.
portion_html: Set the loaded pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide what is left by 14. Scoop that same number into every container so no one gets the light one. Each bowl carries 568 calories and a serious hit of protein, and it reheats better than most roasted vegetables have any right to.

recipeIngredient: Italian seasoning, ground cinnamon, salt and black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 425F and start the cubed sweet potatoes on a sheet pan with oil, italian seasoning and cinnamon for a 15 minute head start.
Toss halved brussels sprouts, red onion wedges and chopped apple with oil and seasoning, and add them to the sweet potato pan.
Toss chunked chicken with oil, garlic and seasoning and spread it in one layer on a second pan.
Roast both pans 18 to 22 minutes until the chicken reads 165F and the sprouts are crisp at the edges.
Fold everything together with the pan juices, then weigh and divide into 14 containers.
